title: HTTP vs HTTPS
definition: HTTP is the foundational protocol for transferring data on the web, operating at the application layer. HTTPS is the secure version, encrypting all communication using TLS/SSL to prevent eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks.
simpleExplanation: HTTP sends your passwords in plain text where anyone on public Wi-Fi can read them. HTTPS scrambles your passwords into an unreadable mess, and only the destination server has the key to unscramble them.

rows: Requires extra RTTs for TLS handshake
